checkpoints.name: Define reusable initialization foundations
checkpoints.scope: Add the shared initialization module and expose reusable state-payload validation without changing the behavior of the existing run, validate, or status commands. Define structured errors and a canonical generated-state shape that satisfies the current plan schema.
exit_criteria: The state validator can validate an in-memory generated payload before it is written
The generated payload includes every required top-level and checkpoint field with pending status, zero attempts, and empty review notes
Protected branches, duplicate checkpoint IDs, and malformed generated payloads produce clear errors
Existing state load/save and loop tests continue to pass
checkpoints.review_notes: Files touched: src/agent_loop/state.py, src/agent_loop/plan_init.py (new), tests/test_state.py, tests/test_plan_init.py (new). state.py: renamed the private `_validate` to a public `validate_payload(raw)` so schema checks run on in-memory dicts, not just files loaded from disk; `load_state` now calls the public function (no behavior change). Added `ProtectedBranchError` and `DuplicateCheckpointError` as InvalidPlanState subclasses and raised them at the existing protected-branch and duplicate-id check sites, so callers that still catch `InvalidPlanState` are unaffected while new code can distinguish failure kinds. plan_init.py: new shared module providing `new_checkpoint(...)` (canonical checkpoint: status=pending, attempts=0, review_notes="") and `build_generated_payload(...)` (canonical top-level shape: plan_file/branch/checkpoints plus optional project/models), and `validate_generated_payload(...)` which reuses state.validate_payload for pre-write validation. Tests added: 12 new (6 in test_plan_init.py covering canonical shape, optional blocks, valid-payload acceptance, protected-branch/duplicate-id/malformed-payload/non-dict rejection, no-disk-IO, and load_state round-trip compatibility; 3 in test_state.py covering the renamed public validate_payload and the two new exception subclasses, plus updated match assertions). Exit criteria: (1) validate_generated_payload/validate_payload validate a plain dict with no Path involved, verified by test_validate_generated_payload_does_not_touch_disk and test_validate_payload_is_reusable_on_in_memory_dict; (2) new_checkpoint/build_generated_payload always emit pending/0/"" fields, verified by test_new_checkpoint_has_canonical_pending_shape; (3) ProtectedBranchError, DuplicateCheckpointError, and generic InvalidPlanState (missing field, non-dict) are raised with clear messages, verified by the corresponding rejection tests; (4) full suite (92 tests, `python3 -m pytest`) passes, including all pre-existing state/orchestrator/cli/provider/example tests.

checkpoints.name: Add captured provider execution and plan generation
checkpoints.scope: Extend the provider layer with a captured-output execution path used only for initialization. Build a strict prompt that converts supplied feature text into ordered, independently reviewable checkpoints and requires JSON-only output. Parse raw or Markdown-fenced JSON and normalize the required initial checkpoint fields.
exit_criteria: The selected provider's stdout and stderr are captured with timeout and non-zero exit handling
The initializer prompt requests project-agnostic, ordered checkpoints with objective exit criteria and no prose outside the JSON result
Raw JSON and a single JSON code fence are accepted, while malformed or mixed output is rejected clearly
The existing streaming Provider.run behavior remains unchanged for the developer/reviewer loop
checkpoints.review_notes: Files touched: src/agent_loop/providers/base.py, src/agent_loop/plan_init.py, tests/test_providers.py, tests/test_plan_init.py (no CLI wiring — that's phase2). base.py: added a `CapturedResult` dataclass (returncode/stdout/stderr/timed_out) and `Provider.run_captured(prompt, timeout)`, a new method that calls `subprocess.run(argv, timeout=timeout, capture_output=True, text=True)` and, on `TimeoutExpired`, returns a `CapturedResult` with `timed_out=True`, `returncode=124`, and whatever partial stdout/stderr the exception carries. `Provider.run` (the streaming path used by run_loop) was not modified at all — only a new method was added alongside it. plan_init.py: added `run_provider_captured(provider, prompt, timeout)`, which calls `run_captured` and raises `ProviderExecutionError` on `timed_out` or non-zero `returncode` (including stderr detail when present) instead of returning a result to parse; added `INIT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`/`build_init_prompt(feature_text)`, a strict prompt requiring 2-6 ordered, project-agnostic, independently reviewable checkpoints with objective exit_criteria, explicitly forbidding status/attempts/review_notes fields (those are assigned by normalization) and forbidding any prose outside a single raw-or-fenced JSON object; added `parse_plan_json(raw_output)`, which counts '```' occurrences to accept raw JSON (0 fences) or exactly one fenced block matched by an anchored regex (2 fences, nothing else in the string), and raises `PlanOutputParseError` with a specific reason for empty output, prose mixed with/around a fence, more than one fence, or invalid JSON; added `normalize_checkpoints(data)`, which accepts `{"checkpoints": [...]}` or a bare list, validates each entry has id/name/scope/exit_criteria (list), and rebuilds every checkpoint via the existing `new_checkpoint` so status/attempts/review_notes are always forced back to the canonical pending/0/"" shape regardless of what the provider returned; added `generate_plan_json(provider, feature_text, timeout)` composing the above for later CLI use. Tests added: 8 in test_providers.py covering run_captured's success/non-zero/timeout/partial-timeout-output/no-stdout-printing paths plus two guard tests pinning that `run`'s subprocess.run(argv, timeout=timeout) call and its 124/print timeout behavior are byte-for-byte unchanged; 29 in test_plan_init.py covering run_provider_captured success/timeout/non-zero(with and without stderr), prompt content (feature text embedded, JSON-only/no-prose wording, project-agnostic/ordered/objective wording), parse_plan_json (raw JSON, fenced with/without 'json' tag, whitespace stripping, empty output, prose before/after raw JSON, prose around/after a fence, >1 fence, invalid JSON raw and inside a fence), normalize_checkpoints (checkpoints-key vs bare-list input, forced canonical shape override, missing/empty/non-dict/missing-field/non-list-exit_criteria rejections), and generate_plan_json end-to-end (success, execution-error propagation, parse-error propagation) using a FakeProvider subclass of Provider. Exit criteria: (1) capture with timeout/non-zero handling — Provider.run_captured plus run_provider_captured's explicit ProviderExecutionError on timed_out/non-zero, verified by the run_captured and run_provider_captured tests; (2) project-agnostic ordered checkpoints with objective exit criteria and no prose outside JSON — verified by the build_init_prompt content tests; (3) raw/fenced JSON accepted, malformed/mixed rejected clearly — verified by the parse_plan_json test matrix (11 cases); (4) existing streaming Provider.run unchanged — verified by the two run()-guard tests plus the fact run() itself was not edited. Full suite: `python3 -m pytest` — 129 passed (92 pre-existing + 37 new), no failures.

checkpoints.name: Implement safe agent-loop init CLI workflow
checkpoints.scope: Add the init subcommand. Accept either a plain-English positional feature description or a Markdown feature file, resolve branch and plan-file defaults, invoke the selected planning provider, validate the result, and write formatted JSON atomically only when it is valid. Protect existing files unless --force is present.
exit_criteria: agent-loop init accepts plain-English input and --feature-file input with unambiguous validation of mutually exclusive arguments
CLI flags support state path, branch, plan-file, provider, model, timeout, and force behavior
A Markdown source path is used as the default plan_file and a plain-English feature receives the documented default plan path
Branch defaults are sanitized feature/<slug> values and protected branches are rejected
No state file is created or replaced when generation, parsing, or validation fails; existing files require --force
checkpoints.review_notes: Files touched: src/agent_loop/plan_init.py, src/agent_loop/cli.py, tests/test_plan_init.py, tests/test_cli.py (no README changes — that's phase3). plan_init.py: added DEFAULT_PLAN_FILE = "docs/implementation_plan.md" (matches the README schema example, used as the default plan_file for plain-English input); slugify(text, max_len=40), which lowercases, collapses any run of non-alphanumeric characters to a single hyphen, strips leading/trailing hyphens (including after truncation), and falls back to "feature" if nothing alphanumeric survives; write_generated_payload(path, payload), which creates parent dirs, writes formatted JSON (indent=2 + trailing newline) to a temp file in the same directory via tempfile.mkstemp, then os.replace()s it into place — on any exception the temp file is unlinked and the original (if any) is left untouched, so a write never leaves a truncated or partial state file. cli.py: added the `init` subparser with a positional `feature` (nargs="?") plus --feature-file, --state, --branch, --plan-file, --provider (choices=known_provider_names(), default claude), --model, --timeout (default 1800), and --force; added _cmd_init, which (1) validates exactly one of feature text / --feature-file is given (clear, distinct error messages for "both" vs "neither"), (2) for --feature-file requires the file exist and be non-empty, reads it as the feature text, and defaults plan_file to str(feature_file) and the branch slug source to the file's stem; for plain-English input defaults plan_file to plan_init.DEFAULT_PLAN_FILE and the slug source to the feature text itself; (3) resolves branch as --branch or f"feature/{slugify(slug_source)}"; (4) rejects a protected branch (checked against state.PROTECTED_BRANCHES) before ever invoking the provider — fails fast, no subprocess call, no file touched; (5) refuses an existing --state path unless --force is given, checked before provider invocation; (6) resolves the provider via get_provider(args.provider, args.model), runs preflight, then generate_plan_json -> normalize_checkpoints -> build_generated_payload -> validate_generated_payload, catching ProviderExecutionError / PlanOutputParseError / InvalidPlanState (which covers ProtectedBranchError and DuplicateCheckpointError as schema-level subclasses) and printing `error: ...` with rc=2 on any of them; (7) only calls write_generated_payload after validation succeeds, so no state file is ever created or replaced on any failure path, regardless of --force. Tests added: 12 in test_plan_init.py (6 for slugify covering lowercasing/hyphenation, punctuation-run collapsing, leading/trailing trim, max_len truncation, truncation not leaving a trailing hyphen, and the "feature" fallback for empty/non-alphanumeric input; 5 for write_generated_payload covering formatted-JSON-with-trailing-newline output, overwriting an existing file, creating nested parent directories, leaving no stray .tmp files behind, and — by monkeypatching json.dump to raise — that a mid-write failure leaves the original file byte-for-byte untouched with no tmp file left behind); 23 in test_cli.py using a _FakeInitProvider (a real Provider subclass with a no-op preflight and a scriptable run_captured) routed in via monkeypatching cli.get_provider, covering: plain-English input writing the default plan_file/branch, --feature-file input using the file path as plan_file and its stem as the branch slug source, rejection of both-given and neither-given (distinct stderr messages), missing/empty --feature-file rejection, every flag override (--branch/--plan-file/--provider/--model/--timeout, asserting the fake provider recorded the right name/model/timeout), existing-state refusal without --force (file byte-for-byte unchanged) and success with --force, protected-branch rejection for both "main" and "master" with an assertion that the provider is never called (fail-fast), no-state-file-written on provider non-zero exit / timeout / malformed (non-JSON) output / schema validation failure (duplicate checkpoint ids) all individually, no-overwrite-of-an-existing-file-on-failure-even-with---force, missing-provider-binary rejection (preflight raising ProviderError), unknown --provider being rejected by argparse choices, and an end-to-end check that a freshly generated state file loads and passes through `agent-loop validate` and `agent-loop status`. Exit criteria: (1) unambiguous mutually-exclusive validation — verified by test_init_rejects_both_feature_and_feature_file and test_init_rejects_neither_feature_nor_feature_file; (2) all six flags present and wired — verified by test_init_flags_override_branch_plan_file_provider_model_timeout plus the --state/--force tests; (3) Markdown source as default plan_file vs. the documented default plan path — verified by test_init_accepts_feature_file_and_uses_it_as_default_plan_file and test_init_accepts_plain_english_and_writes_default_plan_file; (4) sanitized feature/<slug> branch defaults and protected-branch rejection — verified by the slugify unit tests plus test_init_rejects_protected_branch (parametrized main/master, fails before touching the provider); (5) no state file created/replaced on any failure and --force required for existing files — verified by the provider-failure/timeout/malformed-output/schema-failure tests, the force-required test, and the fails-even-with-force test. Manually smoke-tested outside pytest with a real subprocess (a shell script on PATH standing in for `claude`) confirming init writes a schema-valid file that `agent-loop validate` accepts, that a second init without --force is refused with the original file left intact, that --force overwrites, and that --branch main is refused pre-provider-call. Full suite: `python3 -m pytest` — 159 passed (129 pre-existing + 30 new), no failures.

checkpoints.name: Test and document initialization
checkpoints.scope: Add deterministic unit and CLI tests using mocked provider execution, then document the new workflow and safety behavior in the README.
exit_criteria: Tests cover text and Markdown inputs, flag defaults and overrides, valid raw/fenced JSON, malformed output, provider failure/timeout, schema rejection, and overwrite protection
A successfully generated file loads through load_state and works with agent-loop validate and status
README documents text and Markdown init examples, provider/model selection, and --force overwrite behavior
checkpoints.review_notes: Files touched: tests/test_cli.py, README.md (no source changes — phase1/phase2 had already added the bulk of the mocked-provider test suite as part of their own scope; this phase closed the remaining gaps and added documentation). test_cli.py: extended test_init_accepts_plain_english_and_writes_default_plan_file with explicit assertions that unflagged init calls default to provider='claude', model=None, and timeout=1800 (previously only overrides were asserted, not defaults); added test_init_accepts_fenced_json_output, a new CLI-level (not just unit-level) test that feeds a FakeInitProvider a ```json-fenced plan and asserts init still writes a valid, canonical-shape state file end to end. README.md: fixed a pre-existing unclosed code fence (the 'Usage' block opened at line 28 was never closed, so '### Choosing the model' and the safety-env table were being swallowed into the shell code block instead of rendering as prose/headings — added the missing closing ``` after the `agent-loop run` examples); added a new '## Generating a plan (`agent-loop init`)' section with a plain-English example, a --feature-file Markdown example, a flag/default table (--state, --branch, --plan-file, --provider, --model, --timeout, --force), a combined-flags example, prose on overwrite protection and protected-branch rejection, and an end-to-end `init && validate && status` example. Exit criteria: (1) text/Markdown inputs, flag defaults/overrides, raw/fenced JSON, malformed output, provider failure/timeout, schema rejection, and overwrite protection are all covered by mocked-provider tests — text: test_init_accepts_plain_english_and_writes_default_plan_file; Markdown: test_init_accepts_feature_file_and_uses_it_as_default_plan_file; defaults: the same plain-English test now asserts provider/model/timeout defaults; overrides: test_init_flags_override_branch_plan_file_provider_model_timeout; raw JSON: test_init_accepts_plain_english_and_writes_default_plan_file (via _plan_json, raw) plus the parse_plan_json raw-JSON unit tests in test_plan_init.py; fenced JSON: the new test_init_accepts_fenced_json_output (CLI-level) plus the existing parse_plan_json fenced-JSON unit tests; malformed output: test_init_does_not_write_state_on_malformed_output; provider failure: test_init_does_not_write_state_on_provider_failure; timeout: test_init_does_not_write_state_on_provider_timeout; schema rejection: test_init_does_not_write_state_on_schema_validation_failure (duplicate ids) plus test_init_rejects_protected_branch; overwrite protection: test_init_refuses_existing_state_without_force, test_init_overwrites_existing_state_with_force, and test_init_does_not_overwrite_existing_file_on_failure_even_with_force; (2) generated-file usability — verified by test_init_generated_state_is_usable_by_validate_and_status, which runs `init` then feeds the same --state path through `agent-loop validate` and `agent-loop status` via cli.main and checks both succeed and print the expected checkpoint; (3) full suite passes — `python3 -m pytest` reports 160 passed, 0 failures; (4) README documents text/Markdown examples, provider/model selection, and --force behavior — verified by reading the rendered '## Generating a plan' section added above. Full suite: `python3 -m pytest` — 160 passed (159 pre-existing + 1 net new test; the defaults assertions were added to an existing test rather than a new one).
